review_response.rationale: The program applies a strictly greater-than 15 percent threshold to either capital or profits, matching the authority clause.

The update path invokes the upload solely when updated information is received, and the upload routine checks only for a nonblank customer ID. No receipt date, elapsed-time calculation, or control enforces completion within the required 7-day period.
The program uploads the update when updated information is received (src-28f6e6298912, lines 14-15) and imposes no time-bound deadline, matching the authority version's no-deadline requirement.

The authority requires beneficial-owner identification when either capital entitlement or profit entitlement is strictly greater than 15%. The ownership-basis branch evaluates only one measure, so a customer exceeding the threshold on the unselected measure can be incorrectly classified as not a beneficial owner.

The program calculates the deadline by adding one calendar month rather than 30 elapsed days. Because calendar months vary in length, this can produce a deadline more than 30 days after complaint lodging, contrary to the maximum permitted period.

The program retains a 15 percent legacy threshold and applies a strictly-greater comparison to both capital and profit percentages. The current authority requires beneficial-owner identification when either percentage is strictly greater than 10 percent, so interests above 10 percent through 15 percent are incorrectly excluded.

The routine adds one to the month and preserves the original day without normalizing for the destination month's length. Complaints lodged near month-end can therefore produce impossible due dates such as 20230231, so the one-calendar-month boundary is implemented incorrectly.

The program applies a strictly-greater-than 15 percent threshold to both profit entitlement and capital ownership, while the current authority requires a strictly-greater-than 10 percent threshold. This is a stale implementation of the pre-amendment threshold.

The calendar-month deadline calculation treats every year divisible by four as a leap year. It omits the Gregorian century exception, so dates rolling into February 2100, 2200, or 2300 can produce February 29 and exceed the correct one-month boundary by a day.

The submission logic marks an update as submitted when an update was received and a submission ID exists, but it contains no rule or date calculation enforcing submission to the registry within 7 days of receipt.

The upload logic reacts to a received-update flag and marks the record uploaded, but it contains no date capture, elapsed-time calculation, or enforcement of the required maximum seven-day update window.

The calculation advances the complaint date by one calendar month while retaining the day of month, rather than adding at most 30 days. This can produce a 31-day interval and can also create invalid dates, so it does not reliably enforce the authority's maximum 30-day boundary.
T6V2BOSV identifies a beneficial owner when either capital ownership or profit entitlement is strictly greater than 15 percent, matching the authority's threshold and comparator.

The program applies a strictly-greater-than 15 percent threshold to both capital ownership and profit entitlement, while the cited authority requires a strictly-greater-than 10 percent threshold. The implemented comparator is correct, but the threshold is stale.

The queue-processing flow accepts a customer identifier and uploads the record without capturing when updated information was received or enforcing the required maximum seven-day update period. The mandated temporal rule is therefore missing.

February is always capped at 28 days, so complaints lodged on January 29 in a leap year receive a February 28 due date instead of February 29. This miscomputes the one-calendar-month boundary for leap years.

The beneficial-owner test uses a strictly-greater-than 15 percent threshold for both capital and profits, while the current authority requires a strictly-greater-than 10 percent threshold. This is a stale pre-amendment threshold.

The source implements an event-triggered upload when updated customer information is received and encodes no time-bound deadline, consistent with the cited 2018 authority state in which clause (h) required updating upon receipt or periodic updation but prescribed no fixed completion interval.

The authority requires beneficial-owner identification when either capital entitlement or profit entitlement is strictly greater than 15 percent. The program makes the two tests mutually exclusive based on WS-OWNERSHIP-BASIS, so it can omit a qualifying capital interest when the basis is 'P' or a qualifying profit interest otherwise. The missing rule is a combined capital-or-profits evaluation.

The program records a submitted audit status when updated information is received and a submission identifier exists, without imposing any time-bound deadline. This is consistent with the authority's no-deadline requirement.

The program computes the deadline by adding one calendar month rather than exactly 30 days, producing intervals of 28, 29, 30, or 31 days and therefore violating the authority's maximum 30-day period.
The program uploads each queued customer record without encoding or enforcing any time-bound update deadline, which is consistent with the cited authority's no-deadline requirement.
